one_liner: Senior VA contracting officer-level specialist who writes, negotiates and administers $30M–$100M architect-engineer and construction contracts for veterans' facilities under the FAR and VAAR.
fit_summary: This GS-14 role requires an active FAC-C (Professional), four or more years of contracting including a year of GS-13-level architect-engineer and construction contract negotiation, and 24 business-related semester hours. Daniel has no FAC-C, and his contracting-related work at IEM was contractor-side proposals and purchasing, so the selective placement factor screens him out.
eligibility: Open to the public (U.S. citizens) and federal transition candidates; status is not required.
Selective Placement Factor: active FAC-C (Professional) at the time of application, or you are found ineligible.

GS-1102 requirements: 4 years of contracting or related experience plus a 4-year degree with at least 24 semester hours in accounting, business, finance, law, contracts, economics, management or related fields (transcript required).

One year of specialized experience at the GS-13 level leading A-E and construction contract negotiations and applying FAR/VAAR, pricing arrangements and procurement law; no education substitution at GS-14.
Financial disclosure report, background investigation, online assessment and a 1-year probationary period.
strategy: Skip this one: it requires an active FAC-C (Professional) certification at the time of application, and he doesn't have one.
Aim for entry-level GS-7/9 Contract Specialist (1102) roles open to the public, or contracting-adjacent roles in emergency management grants and program analysis.
interview_questions: Walk us through how you planned and led negotiations on a complex architect-engineer or construction contract.
When would you choose an FPIF or CPIF arrangement over firm-fixed-price, and how would you justify it?
Describe a time you resolved a contracting issue not clearly addressed by the FAR or agency guidance.
How do you advise a program customer who wants a requirement that conflicts with small business or competition rules?
watch_outs: Active FAC-C (Professional) is required at application; without it you are automatically ineligible.
Not remote: ad hoc telework only, location set by vacancy, with recurring construction site inspections and a financial disclosure requirement.
GS-14 assumes years of senior contracting experience; your policy and people skills alone will not meet the specialized experience.
